text: True or False: Proof by contrapositive proves P → Q by instead proving ¬Q → ¬P, justified by the classical equivalence (P → Q) ≡ (¬Q → ¬P).
explanation: True. This is exactly the contrapositive strategy and its justification; the two implications are logically equivalent, so proving one proves the other. It is distinct from proving the converse Q → P, which is not equivalent to P → Q.
